articleMarkdown:
# Four of Pentacles: Keeping What Matters Without Losing Room to Move

Protect what you have while checking whether you can still move freely.

Keywords: Preservation · Boundaries · Holding tight

Upright at a glance: Identify what is worth keeping and set boundaries that help you feel secure.

Reversed at a glance: Holding too tightly can stop life moving; loosening a boundary abruptly can also make it hard to restore.

The Four of Pentacles places all four discs against the body: one above the head, one at the chest and two underfoot. Everything seems safe. But what would this person have to do before standing up?

## The body becomes a frame for keeping the pentacles

A crowned figure sits facing forward on a stone seat, wearing a red robe and dark outer garment. Both arms circle a large pentacle at the chest; another stands above the crown, and each foot rests on one. The discs occupy the head, hands and feet in a tightly arranged vertical composition.

A city spreads behind the figure, with towers, walls and red roofs. The figure sits apart on open ground in front of it, with no one else interacting. What we can see is stillness and a firm hold. Fear of loss is an interpretation prompted by that posture, not direct knowledge of the person's thoughts. [View the card image](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pents04.jpg)

## Holding on has a direct basis in the text

Waite briefly describes the figure as holding to what is already possessed. His upright meanings concern secure possessions, attachment to what one has, gifts and inheritance. Reversed, he gives suspense, delay and opposition, rather than directly stating the familiar modern idea of “letting go.”

This article extends preservation to time, access, belongings and personal limits. The reversal checks boundaries that are too tight or too loose. This is a contemporary reflective method, not a rewritten list presented as Waite's original. [Check Waite’s text](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktpe04.htm)

## Upright Keep what genuinely matters

The upright card need not immediately mean stinginess. During change, keeping a familiar space, reducing extra commitments or giving important belongings a fixed place may provide real stability. Ask what you are protecting before deciding whether the boundary fits.

A useful boundary can be explained and adjusted. You might reserve part of each day for taking no new tasks while agreeing how urgent matters should reach you. It protects your capacity to keep living; it need not seal off every contact.

## Reversed Notice the cost of control

If fear of mistakes means everything must go through you, safekeeping can become a bottleneck. You retain decision-making power but lose rest and room to collaborate. Distinguish responsibilities you truly cannot pass on from work someone else could handle under clear rules.

Alternatively, fear of seeming ungenerous may lead you to accept requests beyond your capacity. Letting go also needs limits: when will a borrowed item return, or how far may someone use shared material? Clear terms are steadier than swinging between total restriction and total openness.

## Allowing protection and movement together

A team lead can start by handing over one low-risk task with agreed check-in points. When sorting possessions, distinguish useful items, keepsakes and things kept “just in case,” then decide item by item.

In a relationship, a need for solitude can be stated with a time and reason. Silence or repeated testing to make sure someone will not leave may create a sense of control without genuine reassurance.

## Practice Give a boundary a reason

Complete these sentences: “I want to keep … because it helps me …” and “I can make … available, provided that …” If the reason is simply “I must control everything,” look again for a more specific need that can be discussed.

## Common misreading

The Four of Pentacles neither labels someone a miser nor asks you to immediately discard or surrender everything. The question is whether a boundary serves an actual need and whether its cost remains manageable.

## Sources and image

The image was drawn by Pamela Colman Smith. The source manuscript was based on inspection of the current original JPEG file; version details come from the [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pents04.jpg).

The historical discussion follows [this card’s English entry](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktpe04.htm) in Part III, Section 2 of A. E. Waite’s The Pictorial Key to the Tarot. The source is the English transcription labelled [1911] by the Internet Sacred Text Archive. A physical 1910 first edition was not checked for this batch. The everyday situations, questions and exercises are original modern reflections, not direct translations of Waite’s book.

sourceRecord.title: 星币四 守住需要的也留一点活动空间
sourceRecord.oneLiner: 保护已有的东西，同时看看自己是否还能自由行动。
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 明确什么值得保留，建立让自己安心的边界。
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 握得过紧让生活停住，或边界一松就难以收回。
sourceRecord.hook: 星币四的人把四枚圆盘都安排到身体上：头顶一枚，胸前一枚，脚下两枚。东西似乎很安全，可是他若想起身，要先做什么？

sections.title: 身体成了保管星币的架子
paragraphs: 一个戴冠人物正面坐在石座上，穿红色衣袍、披深色外衣。双臂围住胸前的大星币，冠上立着另一枚，双脚各踩一枚。圆盘分别占据头、手和脚的位置，形成很紧的纵向布局。
身后铺开一座城市，有塔楼、城墙和红色屋顶，人物却坐在城景前方的空地上，没有人与他互动。我们能看见的是静止与紧抱；“害怕失去”是由姿态引出的解释，不能当成已经读到人物内心的事实。 [查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pents04.jpg)

sections.title: 持守有直接文本依据
paragraphs: Waite 用简短的句子概括人物在守住所拥有的东西，正位涉及财产的稳固、执着于已有，以及礼物和传承等旧义。逆位则写悬而未决、延迟与阻力，未直接等同于现代常见的“放手”。
本篇把守成延伸到时间、权限、物品与个人界限；逆位用来检查边界太紧或太松。这是一种当代反思方法，而不是将旧词表改写后仍称为原文。 [核对 Waite 原文](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktpe04.htm)

sections.title: 正位 留住真正重要的部分
paragraphs: 正位不必一上来就被判为吝啬。经历变化时，保留熟悉的空间、减少额外承诺、让重要物品有固定位置，都可能提供实际的稳定。先问自己在保护什么，再决定这道边界是否合适。
好的边界可以说明，也可以调整。比如每天留出不接新任务的时段，同时约定紧急情况如何联系。它保护你继续生活的能力，不需要把所有接触都封住。

sections.title: 逆位 留意控制付出的代价
paragraphs: 若因为担心出错，任何事都必须经过自己，保管就可能变成瓶颈。你守住了决定权，却失去休息和协作的空间。先区分真正不可交出的责任，与别人可以按清楚规则承担的部分。
另一种情况是为避免显得小气，突然答应超出能力的要求。松手也需要范围：借出的物品何时归还，允许别人使用的资料到哪里为止。清楚表达比一会儿全收紧、一会儿全放开更稳定。

sections.title: 保护与流动怎样同时存在
paragraphs: 团队负责人可以先交出一项低风险任务，并约定检查点，练习让别人接手。个人整理时，把有用、纪念和“也许将来有用”的物品分开，再逐一决定。
关系里，需要独处可以直接说出时间和原因。若用不回应、反复试探来确保对方不会离开，控制感未必能带来真正的安心。

sections.title: 练习 给一道边界加上理由
paragraphs: 完成两句话：“我想保留的是……，因为它帮助我……”“我可以开放的是……，前提是……”如果理由只剩“所有事情都得由我掌握”，就再找一个更具体、可讨论的需要。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 星币四既不能凭一张牌给人贴“守财奴”标签，也不要求你立即丢弃或交出所有东西。重点在边界是否支持现实需要，以及守住它的成本是否仍可承受。
